section_summary: This section contains Parker Pen Company exhibits concerning two Japanese fountain pen applications and its opposition to the “Park” and “Park Minor” trade marks. The company argues that Japanese examiners denied protection despite claimed technical differences, foreign patent grants, and the risk of confusing buyers. The section includes patent notices and specifications, opposition decisions, correspondence, drawings, and two statements assembled for a broader protest.

subfiles.title: Bureau notice on utility model application No. 10637
subfiles.about: The bureau requests amendments distinguishing the application from British patent No. 318,982.
subfiles.summary: Requests clearer operational and structural distinctions from the British patent and a punctuation correction.

subfiles.title: Japanese utility model reference and drawings
subfiles.about: A Japanese certified reference copy and technical drawings accompany the Parker utility model papers.
subfiles.summary: A Japanese certification dated August 21, 1935 is followed by largely unreadable text and numbered fountain pen drawings. The reference appears to concern the prior utility model cited elsewhere as No. 35069.

subfiles.title: British patent No. 318,982, Improvements in or relating to Fountain Pens
subfiles.about: The specification describes a spring operated fountain pen filling device used as a comparison for Parker's Japanese application.
subfiles.summary: The partially legible British specification describes a diaphragm seal, plunger, spring, cap, and several filling device variations. Its figures and mechanisms are repeatedly compared with Parker's Japanese utility model. The visible page gives January 23, 1930 as the acceptance date.

subfiles.title: Instructions distinguishing Parker's utility model from prior pens
subfiles.about: The writers propose a restricted claim for a lock that prevents sudden spring driven sleeve movement.
subfiles.summary: Compares Parker's sleeve and pin arrangement with British patent No. 318,982 and Japanese utility model No. 35069. It asks de Havilland to claim the enlarged slot and argue that the lock controls release of the spring driven sleeve.

subfiles.title: Sasaki's opposition to utility model application No. 10637
subfiles.about: Sasaki seeks rejection of Parker's fountain pen utility model for lack of novelty.
subfiles.summary: Sasaki compares four features of Parker's design with British patent No. 318,982 and Japanese utility model No. 35069. He also alleges that Kozo Ishii had manufactured and sold a similar pen since about 1930 and offers him as a witness.

subfiles.title: Instructions to defend Parker's utility model
subfiles.about: The writers instruct de Havilland to defend application No. 10637 against Sasaki's opposition.
subfiles.summary: The letter argues that Parker's preassembled diaphragm mount, rubber washer, spring follower, and lock for a spring driven plunger differ from the cited devices. It says these features improve assembly and durability and merit utility model protection. The final page appears twice, on pages 85 and 86.

subfiles.title: Statement on the PARKER, Park, and Park Minor trade marks
subfiles.about: Parker argues that Japanese acceptance of “Park” and “Park Minor” threatens its registered “PARKER” mark.
subfiles.summary: This statement traces Parker's opposition from its October 1935 cable through adverse decisions and later cancellation efforts. It argues that the marks could confuse buyers of fountain pens and criticizes the Japanese Patent Office's treatment of an American company's registrations. It also reports that the competing applicant was a horticulturist and describes claimed commercial harm.

subfiles.title: Cable ordering opposition to Park and Park Minor
subfiles.about: The cable instructs opposition to two advertised trade mark applications.
subfiles.summary: Orders opposition to “Park” and “Park Minor” based on Parker registrations 150273 and 171867.

subfiles.title: Confirmation of instructions to oppose Park and Park Minor
subfiles.about: The writers confirm the cable and identify the applicant and registrations supporting opposition.
subfiles.summary: Names Keikichi Taketomi as applicant and asks the Japanese attorneys to oppose both Class 51 marks.

subfiles.title: Report that trade mark oppositions were filed
subfiles.about: The Japanese attorneys confirm filing oppositions to the two Taketomi applications.
subfiles.summary: Lists the application and advertisement numbers and argues that both marks resemble “PARKER.”

subfiles.title: Decision rejecting opposition to Park Minor
subfiles.about: The examiner rejects Parker's opposition to Taketomi's “Park Minor” application.
subfiles.summary: Finds “Park Minor” and “Parker” different in sound and appearance and unlikely to confuse buyers.

subfiles.title: Decision rejecting opposition to Park
subfiles.about: The examiner rejects Parker's opposition to Taketomi's “Park” application.
subfiles.summary: Finds “Park” distinguishable from “Parker” in sound, appearance, and idea.

subfiles.title: Instructions for appeal of the trade mark decisions
subfiles.about: The writers instruct an appeal against rejection of Parker's trade mark oppositions.
subfiles.summary: The letter argues that “Park” and “Park Minor” would confuse purchasers of fountain pens bearing the established “PARKER” name. It discusses protection of both the mark owner and the public, offers analogies involving other marks, and questions Taketomi's reason for choosing the words. It asks the Japanese attorneys to seek reversal and advise whether evidence is needed.

subfiles.title: Report on registration status of Park and Park Minor
subfiles.about: The Japanese attorneys report that neither challenged mark is yet registered.
subfiles.summary: Promises another records check and an inquiry into Taketomi's activities.

subfiles.title: Report identifying Taketomi as a horticulturist
subfiles.about: The Japanese attorneys report Taketomi's occupation.
subfiles.summary: States that Taketomi is a horticulturist and questions his interest in stationery marks.

subfiles.title: Report of cancellation proceedings against Park and Park Minor
subfiles.about: The Japanese attorneys report filing cancellation proceedings against the registered marks.
subfiles.summary: Identifies the new registration numbers, argues that the marks resemble “PARKER,” and requests powers of attorney and corporate nationality certificates.

subfiles.title: Statement on rejection of Parker's striped pen barrel application
subfiles.about: Parker challenges the Japanese rejection of its application for a barrel with alternating transparent and opaque sections.
subfiles.summary: The statement reviews Japanese bureau notices, Parker's replies, and cited utility models in the application identified elsewhere as No. 12149. It contrasts the rejection with patent grants or acceptance abroad, arguing that the examiner's objections were vague and missed the claimed striped structure. It says Japanese imitations increased Parker's enforcement costs in Asian and other markets.

subfiles.title: Marking Device specification
subfiles.about: The specification claims a fountain pen barrel made from alternating transparent and opaque material.
subfiles.summary: Describes laminated pyroxylin sheets formed into rods or ribbons and then into pen barrels. Transparent sections show the ink level while opaque sections produce a patterned appearance. Six claims cover the resulting holder and methods of making it.

subfiles.title: First bureau notice on application No. 12149
subfiles.about: The bureau finds Parker's alternating transparent and opaque sheets insufficiently novel.
subfiles.summary: Cites Japanese utility model No. 40634 and common practice in making striped patterns.

subfiles.title: Instructions replying to the first bureau notice
subfiles.about: The writers propose amended claims and distinguish Parker's barrel from a cited Japanese utility model.
subfiles.summary: Explains the visibility and construction advantages of alternating transparent and opaque zones over a narrow barrel window. Proposes replacement claims covering the pen and the method of forming its laminated barrel.

subfiles.title: Second bureau notice on application No. 12149
subfiles.about: The bureau again declines acceptance, citing transparent barrels and a prior graduated window.
subfiles.summary: Cites Japanese utility model publication No. 8138 against Parker's opaque zones.

subfiles.title: Drawing of cited Japanese utility model No. 40634
subfiles.about: The drawing supplies a visual reference for the utility model cited in the first bureau notice.
subfiles.summary: Two figures depict the cited fountain pen barrel construction.

subfiles.title: Japanese utility model publication No. 8138
subfiles.about: The cited Japanese publication describes a fountain pen with a graduated transparent window.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese text and drawings concern a “meter” fountain pen whose transparent insert shows the amount of ink remaining.

subfiles.title: Instructions replying to the second bureau notice
subfiles.about: The writers urge another argument for the benefits of narrow alternating opaque and transparent zones.
subfiles.summary: Distinguishes Parker's barrel from utility model No. 8138's single transparent insert and asks de Havilland to seek allowance of the restricted claims. The letter continues beyond this section.
